macro.headline: Tape splits — Dow and defensives lead, tech and metals bleed.
macro.story:
The facts first: SPY closed at $750.72, down 0.5% on the day but still above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages, with RSI at a middling 54.7. QQQ diverged sharply — down 1.6% on the day and 2.4% over five days, sitting below its 50-day, with RSI at 45.6 and MACD rolling bearish. The Dow is holding up (+1.7% over 21 days) while Nasdaq lags (-3.0% over 21 days). VIX jumped to 18.32, up nearly 22% in five days and 9.5% on the day alone. Gold has fallen 7.8% over 21 days and silver has cratered 20.6% over the same window, both with RSI in the mid-30s and below their 200-day. WTI oil is up 12.4% over five days to $80.23. The 10-year yield is climbing (4.57%, up 2.2% over 21 days), the 2s10s curve is steepening, and DXY is firm at 100.8, up 1.3% on the month. S&P 500 breadth is balanced at 33% bullish versus 29% bearish; 7 of 11 GICS sectors sit above their 50-day.

The tracked conversation leans bearish on the causal read, and the substance points to a specific cocktail: a high-profile earnings disappointment in mega-cap streaming triggering a growth-tape reset, sharp downside in memory-chip names dragging the Nasdaq futures lower, an ongoing Iran conflict keeping a geopolitical risk premium in the tape, and a China GDP print (+4.3% year-on-year in Q2) undershooting Beijing's own target range. Chart reads within the pulse describe the Nasdaq 100 futures printing lower highs and lower lows into a marked support shelf, and a streaming-name breakdown with no reversal structure. A bullish minority in the pulse is picking through specific single names (semis, small-caps, a few consumer plays) rather than defending the index. This attributed narrative is consistent with what the price data shows: tech-led weakness, a VIX bid, curve steepening on rising long-end yields, and defensives (Staples, Real Estate, Utilities) holding up while Tech, Materials, and the Nasdaq 100 sit in bearish momentum status. Sentiment and tape agree — this is a growth-leadership problem, not a broad risk-off.

Underneath the index, rotation is doing real work. Consumer Staples, Real Estate, Energy, and Financials are all in HOT status with bullish MACD; Healthcare, Utilities, Communication Services, and the S&P 500 itself are qualifying bullish. Technology, Nasdaq 100, and Materials are the bearish trio. That is a classic late-cycle-rotation footprint — money is not leaving equities, it is moving inside them. The DXY firmness and rising real yields explain the gold and silver bleed via the validated dollar-strength/metals headwind. The oil bounce sits against an active theme of geopolitical risk (Iran strikes), which per the active-themes data, not live sentiment, would normally unwind lower — the current tape is pricing the risk back in.

Forward watch: whether QQQ can reclaim its 50-day, whether VIX crosses 20 (which would cap confidence lower and change the sizing regime), and whether the Early-Runway rotation into Refiners, Diagnostics, Health Information Services, and Credit Services broadens or fades. Breadth is not washed out and not euphoric — this is a transitional zone where selection matters more than beta.

**[THE SPINE]** The precious-metals unwind is the dominant force this week, and it's radiating outward into a broader dollar-up / commodities-mixed regime. Silver -21% over 21 days, Gold -8%, Copper -4%, DXY grinding +1.3% higher to 100.81 with RSI 54 and holding above its 50-day. This isn't a one-asset story — it's the mirror image of the AI infrastructure chase, where capital is rotating out of hard-asset hedges and into mega-cap compute. Every other read on the tape needs to be filtered through that lens.

**[CROSS-ASSET LENS]** The macro backdrop supports the spine but doesn't extend it aggressively. Regime is CHOPPY (confidence 6/10, transitional), VIX at 18.4 with 21d +16% but still below 20 and term structure roughly flat (VIX/VIX3M 18.4/18.6). The DXY_METALS tag is flagged HOLDS in the backtest — DXY inverse-to-metals is real, and with DXY firming that headwind on Gold/Silver/Copper is live, not noise. Yields firmer across the curve (10Y 4.54, +2.5% on 21d) but the backtest explicitly says do not fade — this is trend, not a ceiling. TLT at 84.2 with RSI 39 looks oversold but the signal DOESN'T HOLD; treat it as downtrend continuation, not a bounce setup.

**[SECTOR & ROTATION LENS]** Leadership is XLF +6.3% and XLV +6.3% over 21d, with XLE +3.4% as the commodity-adjacent survivor. Rotation flow is into Consumer Electronics, Software – Infrastructure, and unmapped names — classic risk-on compute/hardware bid. The FADING tags are loud: Precious Metals complex (GLD/SLV/GDX/GDXJ all accelerating bearish) and Broad Commodity/Agriculture reflation both broke down. The AI Infrastructure Build-Out theme is at CHASING stage, day 46, health 8/10 — mature but still healthy. Nat Gas reversal has two invalidators triggered and is dead for now.

**[WHERE THE OPPORTUNITY IS]** Semiconductors are 13 months hot, +258% — that's the record on file and it carries a CEILING flag. NVDA is coiling 91% with bullish flow, but at the industry level this is exits-not-entries territory; a coiled leader in an extended industry is a trade, not an investment. The cleaner setups are in Software – Infrastructure (1 month hot, only +3% into the spell — early innings) with TWLO (bullish flow, 77% coil) and PLTR (lean bullish, 84% coil), and Internet Content & Information (1 month, -5% into the spell — even earlier) with PINS and META both showing bullish flow and 87–88% coils. These are in-range names with smart-money footprints in industries that have runway; the Semi trade requires tighter risk.

**[WHAT TO WATCH]** The tripwire is DXY 101.80 resistance. A clean break there re-accelerates the metals unwind and likely pressures the coiled-leader setups (compute names are not immune to a real dollar breakout). A rejection back below 100.56 support is the first signal the spine is loosening and metals get a tactical bounce — though remember, 88% of washout lows get retested within 60 days, so even if Silver/Gold bounce here, do not call the low in. Secondary watch: VIX through 19.44 res would tell us the choppy regime is losing its grip.
